niche.habitat: Alpine slopes, cliff edges, wind-exposed ridges, and the rock spire periphery.
niche.diet: Herbivore: high-altitude grasses, mineral licks, and salt spray.
niche.active: Diurnal, most active in clear midday and during evening convection gusts.

body: Tall stilt-walker with elongated metapodials that absorb shock and keep the body clear of ground fog and biting insects. Their neck-sway balance display counters the 1.6× wind force on exposed ridges, while their rhythmic stomp-dance doubles as a ground-drum alarm.

chains.trait: Long metapodial stilt legs, short aerobic sprint
links: Open east meadows offer little cover
Flight beats fight, so selection lengthens stride
1.6 bar drag caps top speed and power demand exceeds aerobic output
Burst capped at ~6 s before lactic acid and traction loss

skill.effect: The creature dashes forward at a remarkable pace for a short while before needing a brief rest. It moves noticeably slower when traversing grassy fields, broken lava crust, or wet mud.

chains.weakness: Wet meadow mud or fractured lava crust breaks metapodial traction and triggers the sprint penalty early; force them onto firm ground or use erratic turning (herd dilution) instead of chasing.

journal.en: Fast for six seconds, then honest about it.

analogues.organism: Cursorial open-habitat ungulates—pronghorn (Antilocapra americana) and springbok (Antidorcas marsupialis) use long limbs and short high-cost bursts on open ground; dense air (F4) strengthens sprint-as-burst vs endurance (from memory, unverified on exact drag scaling).
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: Dawn fog blinds eyes and masks sound
Seismic and low-frequency calls travel through soil and dense air
Four-beat tap at near-max stride amplitude signals neuromuscular precision under 1.05 g
Exposure at dawn forfeits foraging and vigilance exactly when Garfio hunts, making the dance an honest handicap

skill.effect: +10 befriend base (works best on wet compacted meadow; dry ash halves payout); +4 in open midday sun; +18 if the player matches the 4-beat tap; answering an off-tempo rhythm loses the audition.

chains.weakness: Dry loose ash or wind masking breaks the seismic channel and halves befriend payout; drum the beat off-tempo and any Zanco that answers it turns away after 5 s — farm trust from rivals or sabotage an audition.
observe: the herd walks in a slow two-step — the dance is its walk, rehearsed
each lift swings to near-max stride, one slip would be a fall in this gravity
a Garfio thuds the beat off-tempo nearby and a young Zanco freezes

journal.en: It dances its walk. Miss a beat, miss the ground. I drum the wrong rhythm and it walks off.

analogues.organism: Ritualised foot displays: sandhill crane lek stepping; ruffed grouse (Bonasa umbellus) log-drumming; substrate-coupled low-frequency courtship parallels elephant infrasonic/seismic signalling (O'Connell-Rodwell et al., 2000, unverified year detail). Dense dawn fog (F8) + low-frequency carry (F4) make vibratory/foot rhythm a credible dual-channel signal.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: Tall grass and dense air muffle high-frequency calls
A sharp stomp sends a seismic pulse through soil and a low-frequency acoustic thump through 1.6 bar air
Each Zanco re-stomps the pulse in a relay, amplifying it hop-by-hop
Herd bolts in unison before the predator closes distance

skill.effect: The creature strikes the ground to sound an alarm that quickly rallies nearby herd members to flee. If you stomp nearby, it triggers the warning, but stumbling on ash or snow surfaces will mark you as a threat.

chains.weakness: Soft volcanic ash, deep snow, or a hard rock slab under the herd decouples the seismic pulse and muffles the acoustic thump; cut them off on these substrates or avoid triggering the relay.

plausibility.summary: Cap reliable herd alert to ~80–120 m on cohesion tuff/meadow pan; reserve ~200 m for thin regolith over basalt or packed game trails—soft ash/snow weakness already correct.
fixes: Cap reliable herd alert to ~80–120 m on cohesion tuff/meadow pan; reserve ~200 m for thin regolith over basalt or packed game trails—soft ash/snow weakness already correct.

analogues.organism: African elephant (Loxodonta africana) footfalls and alarm rumbles coupled into substrate; kangaroo rats (Dipodomys) foot-drumming alarm (Randall, 1984, from memory unverified). Low-frequency seismic alarm fits muffled highs in tall grass + thick air (F4, F8).
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Neck-sway balance display in viewpoint gusts
links: Viewpoint gusts shove tall, light frames at 1.6× wind force per m/s
The long neck acts as a dynamic counterbalance while the tail flicks as a fast neuromuscular flag
Phase-locked sway through a gust proves balance under load cannot be faked
Still air gives nothing to imitate, so wind timing sets the display's difficulty

skill.effect: The creature sways its neck in time with passing wind gusts to build trust. You must mirror its movements to strengthen the bond, but missing the rhythm breaks the connection and forces you to start over.

chains.weakness: No wind, no dance: lure them into sheltered calm and the display collapses; a sudden player roar mimics a gust spike and resets their rhythm.
observe: the tail flicks a beat after gust onset
the neck leans into the gust while the small tail damps the wobble

journal.en: It doesn't dance; it refuses to fall. The wind signs the beat, and I hold the phase.

plausibility.summary: Tail flick should lag/react to gust onset (balance correction), not lead it—mates score sustained phase-lock of neck/torso after each perturbation; sheltered calm disabling the display stays as written.
fixes: Tail flick should lag/react to gust onset (balance correction), not lead it—mates score sustained phase-lock of neck/torso after each perturbation; sheltered calm disabling the display stays as written.

analogues.organism: Long-necked birds stabilising in wind—flamingos and swans use neck inertia as dynamic counterbalance; giraffe locomotion/neck inertia trade-offs (Biewener & Daley, 2007, from memory unverified). Honest balance under 1.6× wind load (F19) at exposed ridges is plausible; predictive pre-gust tail beats need this tweak.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

temperament: Nervous but graceful, they communicate through percussive stomps and swaying postures rather than vocalizations.
moments: A sudden stomp-dance that ripples through the herd like a wave, warning of a Garfio raid.
Neck-swaying in unison against the evening convection winds.
A young one slipping on andesite scree and surviving the fall thanks to low terminal velocity.
